text:
Maria C: heads-up — ran a quick smoke on the VanguardX LoRA merge (v2) with int4 quant on dedicated infra, and we're seeing SKU token collapse in transactional outputs. sample below.

Anjali R: ugh. can you paste an example?

Maria C: yes — input and two outputs (fp16 vs int4):

Maria C: INPUT: 'Create order for SKU: VX-129-PLT quantity 3 shipping next-day'

Maria C: FP16 OUTPUT: 'Order created: SKU VX-129-PLT x3. Shipping: Next-day.'

Maria C: INT4 OUTPUT: 'Order created: SKU VX- <unk> quantity 3. Shipping: Next-day.'

TJ: that looks like tokenization/quantization causing split tokens => <unk> or empty token. similar to token stretch issues we've seen. did you run with tokenizer override?

Maria C: default tokenizer on the model. LoRA weights merged via our merge tool + quantize with quant-recipe v0.9 (symmetric).

Oliver H: can you run the focused eval pack I pushed to the VanguardX repo? it checks SKU patterns, numeric fidelity, and short-span tokens. command is:
```bash
redwood eval run --package vanguardx/sku-check --model merged-vx-v2 --quant int4 --seed 42
```

Maria C: running now. sending logs.

EvalBot: eval started (run id: ev-20260321-9). compiling metrics: token_coverage, sku_preserve_rate, numeric_roundtrip_accuracy.

EvalBot: partial results: sku_preserve_rate: 0.38 (target >= 0.95), numeric_roundtrip_accuracy: 0.97, token_coverage: 0.72

Anjali R: yikes 0.38. so numeric handling mostly ok but SKU tokens are lost. suggests vocab/merging problem after quant.

TJ: two likely causes: 1) the LoRA introduces new subtoken patterns that the quantizer mishandles, 2) KV cache truncation + int4 kernel rounding causes early stop of subtoken sequence.

Oliver H: quick mitigation: pin the model to int8 quant variant or use hybrid-quant (embeddings fp16 + attention int4). try running the same eval with --quant int8 and compare.

Maria C: running int8 now.

EvalBot: eval completed (ev-20260321-9b). sku_preserve_rate: 0.96, numeric_roundtrip_accuracy: 0.98, token_coverage: 0.94

Maria C: int8 fixes it. good catch.

Anjali R: long-term we should add a pre-merge quickscan: run sku-check pack across quant targets (fp16,int8,int4) and fail merges that drop sku_preserve_rate below threshold.

TJ: agree. also add a small calibration set of customer-specific tokens (like vendor SKUs) into quantization fine-tuning / tokenizer update step.

Oliver H: operationally: for VanguardX recommend shipping merged-v2 as int8 by default for dedicated, and gate int4 behind canary + sku-preserve SLO. I've noted a rollout flag.

Maria C: I'll open a quick PR to the merge pipeline to run the sku-check eval and surface the three quant metrics in the merge report.

Anjali R: sweet — if you want I can add the token whitelist upload step to onboarding docs so customers can provide critical tokens.

Maria C: thanks — that should prevent surprises. tagging follow-ups: @TJ for quant config, @Oliver H for rollout gating, @Anjali R for docs.

TJ: will prep a small doc with recommended quant recipes and a fallback policy (int4 -> int8 auto-fallback).

EvalBot: note: added ev-20260321-9 and ev-20260321-9b results to the VanguardX project dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/projects/vanguardx/evals/ev-20260321-9

Oliver H: good job catching this early. :thumbsup:

Maria C: thanks team — will update merge status in the PR and block int4 rollout for now.
